ra: Jannah (Paradise) is a principal division of the Islamic otherworldly geography
Jahannam (Hell) is a principal division of the Islamic otherworldly geography
Barzakh is the intermediate realm of the akhira between death and resurrection
As-Sirat, the bridge over Hell, is a threshold structure of the otherworld
al-Aʿraf is the liminal partition within the cosmic geography between Paradise and Hell
Sidrat al-Muntaha marks the cosmic boundary of the seventh heaven within the akhira
Firdaus is the highest level within Jannah
Jannat ʿAdn is a named garden/level of Paradise
Dar al-Salam is an appellation/level of Paradise in classical exegesis
Dar al-Qarar is read as a name/level of the abode of Paradise
The eight gates are the entrances of Jannah
The seven gates structure the levels of Jahannam (Q 15:44)
Lazaa is one of the seven levels/gates of Hell in classical schemes
al-Hutamah is one of the seven levels/gates of Hell
Saʿir is one of the seven levels/gates of Hell
Saqar is one of the seven levels/gates of Hell
al-Jahim is one of the seven levels/gates of Hell
al-Hawiyah, the abyss, is the deepest of the seven levels/gates of Hell
The lote-tree stands beside the Garden of Refuge at the seventh heaven, at the edge of Paradise
As-Sirat is the bridge stretched over Jahannam that the resurrected must cross
al-Aʿraf is the height bordering Paradise, whose occupants long to enter it
al-Aʿraf borders Hell, whose occupants see and shrink from its inhabitants (Q 7:47)
Ridwan is the angel who keeps the gates of Paradise in Islamic tradition
Malik is the angel set over Hellfire (Q 43:77)
The Hur are the companions promised to dwell in Paradise
The bearers of the Throne are situated above the seventh heaven, near the boundary marked by Sidrat al-Muntaha
Munkar questions the dead in the grave, the realm of the Barzakh
Nakir questions the dead in the grave, the realm of the Barzakh
